bandReport.notes:
DECIMAL SEPARATOR: this booklet prints a RAISED MIDDLE DOT (U+00B7), not a full stop. Verified at high zoom on two independent items -- p08 item 15 'dimensions 2·5′ × 8′' and p10 item 20's four options '13·51 / 13·65 / 13·85 / 14·05'. The dot sits at mid-digit height, clearly distinct from the baseline full stop in the same line (e.g. '10′. Two rectangular'). All decimals in this band are transcribed with U+00B7 as printed. No intra-paper inconsistency observed on my pages.

FOOT/PRIME MARKS: items 10, 13 and 15 use a prime for feet (4′, 6′, 5′, 199′, 195′, 1000′, 2′, 15′, 2·5′, 8′, 10′). Transcribed as U+2032 PRIME.

BAND BOUNDARIES: p02 (printed page 3) is the first question page of the paper, so item 1 is whole. p10 (printed page 11) ends cleanly after item 20 with '[ P.T.O.', so item 20 is whole and item 21 begins on p12, which is not mine.

DIRECTIONS BLOCKS -- all four that open on my pages also CLOSE on my pages; none spans into another band.
  * 'Directions for the following 5 (five) items :' (p02-c1 top) -- data sufficiency, governs items 1-5, closes on p02-c2.
  * 'Directions for the next 2 (two) items :' (p02-c2, Kalagram passage) -- governs items 6-7; the passage runs across the p02/p04 page break and the two items sit on p04-c1.
  * 'Directions for the next 2 (two) items :' (p06-c1, Sport passage) -- governs items 11-12.
  * 'Directions for the next 2 (two) items :' (p08-c2, deflation passage) -- governs items 16-17; item 16 is on p08-c2 and item 17 on p10-c1, so this set spans the page break.
Items 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19 and 20 are standalone with no directions block and carry no context.

DATA SUFFICIENCY OPTIONS (items 1-5): the booklet prints the four choices ONCE, inside the directions block, and prints NO (a)-(d) beneath the individual items. The four directions choices are therefore reproduced as options A-D on each of items 1-5, and each item's 'Question :' / 'Statement I :' / 'Statement II :' lines are kept in the STEM (never in context), so the five stems stay distinct and cannot collide on content_hash.

PRINTED ODDITY, item 1 (transcribed as printed, NOT corrected): the stem reads 'X receives three coins of different denominations : 1, 2, 5, 10 and 20' -- three coins but five denominations listed. Verified at high zoom; the wording is the booklet's. It most likely means three coins drawn from that set of denominations, but nothing on the page says so, so it is left exactly as printed.

EMPHASIS, item 7: the booklet sets the word 'not' in bold italic ('which one of the following statements is not correct?'). Transcribed as **not** to preserve the printed emphasis, following the 2019-p1 item 16 precedent in this corpus. A reviewer who prefers the plain-text convention used elsewhere can strip the asterisks without changing meaning.

ITEM 18 STRING: verified character-by-character at 8x zoom. The string is '× b × a × a × × a × a × bab' -- exactly TWO consecutive × between the second and third 'a' (a first, lower-resolution reading suggested three; the zoom settles it at two). Counting characters ignoring spaces gives positions 7 and 8 as that pair of ×, which is consistent with what the item asks about. The × are literal placeholder characters in a character-string puzzle, not multiplication, so they are left as plain U+00D7 rather than wrapped in math delimiters.

COLUMN CROPS: all ten crops were clean and read in c1-then-c2 order. p02-c1 carries a narrow sliver of the neighbouring column down its right edge (isolated letters 'D', 'F', 'i', 'b', 'T', 'M', 'I', 's', 'e'); it clips nothing from c1 itself, and the affected c2 text was read from p02-c2. Structure was cross-checked against the full-page p02.png, which confirms nothing spans the gutter on that page.

No unreadable text, no missing item numbers, no duplicate or blank options, and no other printed defects found in items 1-20.

questions.context:
Directions for the next 2 (two) items :
Read the following passage and answer the items that follow. Your answers should be based solely on the passage.

‘Kalagram’, the cultural village set up at the Maha Kumbh Mela, unfolded as a mosaic of India’s diverse regions, each represented by seven meticulously crafted ‘Sanskriti Angans’—stepping through the grand portal was like entering another world. These thematic zones, inspired by iconic temples like the Dakshineshwar Kali Temple and the Brahma Mandir, were treasure troves of regional artistry. Bengal’s Pattachitra paintings, Assam’s bamboo crafts, Tamil Nadu’s Thanjavur paintings, and Madhya Pradesh’s tribal sculpture—all were showcased in these living galleries where 230 master artisans breathed life into them using age-old techniques, their hands shaping India’s ancient history into creations to behold.
questions.stem:
Which of the following conclusions are valid?
1. Seven Sanskriti Angans, representing different regions of India, had been showcased in Kalagram.
2. Regional artistry was recognised via the inspiration drawn from iconic temples.
3. India’s ancient history had been crafted by the contemporary craftsmanship of 230 artisans into creations to behold.
4. Art forms from all regions of India had been showcased in these living galleries.
Select the answer using the code given below.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 and 2 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2, 3 and 4

options.label: C
options.text: 1, 2 and 4

options.label: D
options.text: 1 and 3

How is deflation done? Most countries use a method called ‘double deflation’, where input and output prices are deflated separately. Consider a manufacturer importing oil for use in production. If oil prices fall, output prices do not and quantities remain the same, real value added should not change. But if the same deflator is used for inputs and outputs, as in India, it would look as if the manufacturer had become more productive.

1. Real value should not change in the instance of static output cost and unchanged quantities against falling oil prices.
2. Deflators are to be used separately for inputs and outputs, and this is a practice universally adopted by all economies.
Select the answer using the code given below.

options.label: A
options.text: 1 only

options.label: B
options.text: 2 only

options.label: C
options.text: Both 1 and 2
